note: Every paper cited in the exercise files, with what it's used for. Each entry's `match` text must appear in at least one `source` field (tests/exercises.test.mjs checks both ways).

references.citation: Anderson DE, Madigan ML, Nussbaum MA (2007). Maximum voluntary joint torque as a function of joint angle and angular velocity: model development and application to the lower limb. J Biomech 40(14):3105–3113.
references.usedFor: Hip, knee and ankle strength curves and peak torques (hip extension and flexion, knee extension and flexion, plantarflexion).

references.citation: Chen Z, Franklin DW (2025). Joint moment–angle/velocity relations in the hip, knee, and ankle: a meta-visualization of datasets. J Biomech 183. Read as the bioRxiv preprint (CC BY 4.0).
references.usedFor: Cross-check of the leg peak strengths against several hundred isometric datasets, normalised by body mass × height; flags the hip adductor peak as high.

references.citation: Lindahl O, Movin A, Ringqvist I (1969/1972). Isometric knee extension strength as a function of joint angle, muscle length and motor unit activity. Acta Orthop Scand 43:138–147.
references.usedFor: Cross-check of the knee-extension curve's shape.

references.citation: Pinter IJ, Bobbert MF, van Soest AJ, Smeets JBJ (2010). Isometric torque–angle relationships of the elbow flexors and extensors in the transverse plane. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 20:923–931.
references.usedFor: Elbow flexion and extension strength curves and peak torques.

references.citation: Mayer F, Horstmann T, Röcker K, Heitkamp HC, Dickhuth HH (1994). Normal values of isokinetic maximum strength, the strength/velocity curve, and the angle at peak torque of all degrees of freedom in the shoulder. Int J Sports Med 15:S19–S25.
references.usedFor: Shoulder peak torques: flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation.

references.citation: Kulig K, Andrews JG, Hay JG (1984). Human strength curves. Exerc Sport Sci Rev 12:417–466.
references.usedFor: Shapes of the shoulder strength curves (flexion, abduction, horizontal adduction, rotation).

references.citation: Haidar SG, Lloyd J, Cox D, Deshmukh S (2009). Shoulder abduction strength: is it affected by the degree of abduction? J Bone Joint Surg Br 91-B Suppl I:160 (conference abstract).
references.usedFor: Shoulder-abduction strength curve (lateral raise).

references.citation: Neumann DA, Soderberg GL, Cook TM (1988). Comparison of maximal isometric hip abductor muscle torques between hip sides. Phys Ther 68(4):496–502.
references.usedFor: Hip-abduction strength curve.

references.citation: Welsh P, Howitt S, Howarth SJ (2020). The influence of hip joint angle on the ratio between adduction and abduction torque in experienced, recreational male ice hockey players. Int J Sports Phys Ther 15(1):22–33.
references.usedFor: Hip abduction and adduction strength vs hip angle.

references.citation: Uritani D, Fukumoto T (2012). Differences of isometric internal and external hip rotation torques among three different hip flexion positions. J Phys Ther Sci 24(9):863–865.
references.usedFor: Hip internal and external rotation strength by hip flexion (3D leg lifts).

references.citation: Lategan L (2002). Normative isokinetic torque values for rehabilitation in South Africa. DPhil thesis, University of Pretoria.
references.usedFor: Shoulder horizontal abduction (rear delts, rows) and horizontal adduction (pecs, bench) peak torques.

references.citation: de Leva P (1996). Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. J Biomech 29(9):1223–1230.
references.usedFor: Segment masses and centres of mass.

references.citation: Guex K, Gojanovic B, Millet GP (2012). Influence of hip-flexion angle on hamstrings isokinetic activity in sprinters. J Athl Train 47(4):390–395.
references.usedFor: Hamstring strength vs hip angle (lying vs seated leg curl).

references.citation: Black SJ, Woodhouse ML, Suttmiller S, Shall L (1993). Influence of hip position on electromyographic and torque productions in the knee flexors and extensors. J Sport Rehabil 2:26–34.
references.usedFor: Hamstrings weaker supine; knee extension unchanged by hip angle.

references.citation: Worrell TW, Perrin DH, Denegar CR (1989). The influence of hip position on quadriceps and hamstring peak torque and reciprocal muscle group ratio values. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 11(3):104–107.
references.usedFor: Hip angle and thigh-muscle strength (cross-check).

references.citation: Bampouras TM, Reeves ND, Baltzopoulos V, Maganaris CN (2017). The role of agonist and antagonist muscles in explaining isometric knee extension torque variation with hip joint angle. Eur J Appl Physiol 117:2039–2045.
references.usedFor: Knee extension unchanged by hip angle (rectus femoris check).

references.citation: Cresswell AG, Löscher WN, Thorstensson A (1995). Influence of gastrocnemius muscle length on triceps surae torque development and electromyographic activity in man. Exp Brain Res 105:283–290.
references.usedFor: Calf strength vs knee angle (standing vs seated calf raise).

references.citation: Baptista MT, Nascimento FXM, Nardes LK, Matta TT, Oliveira LF (2014). Influência de posições do joelho no torque e atividade mioelétrica do tríceps sural na flexão plantar isométrica máxima. Rev Bras Educ Fís Esporte 28(2):197–202.
references.usedFor: Calf strength and gastrocnemius EMG, knee straight vs bent.

references.citation: Kovács B, Csala D, Yang S, Tihanyi J, Gu Y, Hortobágyi T (2024). Knee position affects medial gastrocnemius and soleus activation during dynamic plantarflexion: no evidence for an inter-muscle compensation in healthy young adults. Biol Open 13:bio061810.
references.usedFor: Calf torque and gastrocnemius EMG with the knee bent.

references.citation: Guenzkofer F, Bubb H, Bengler K (2012). Maximum elbow joint torques for digital human models. Int J Human Factors Modelling and Simulation 3(2):109–132.
references.usedFor: Elbow strength by shoulder angle, elbow angle and grip (curls, triceps, pull-ups, pulldowns).

references.citation: Kohn S, Smart RR, Jakobi JM (2018). Voluntary activation and twitch potentiation of the elbow flexors across supinated, neutral, and pronated forearm orientations. Physiol Rep 6(1):e13560.
references.usedFor: Elbow-flexion strength by grip.

references.citation: Mandalidis DG, O'Brien M (2001). Isokinetic strength of the elbow flexors with the forearm in supination and in the neutral position. Isokinetics and Exercise Science 9:111–117.
references.usedFor: Neutral vs palms-up elbow-flexion strength.

references.citation: Kleiber T, Kunz L, Disselhorst-Klug C (2015). Muscular coordination of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion with respect to hand position. Front Physiol 6:215.
references.usedFor: Biceps and brachioradialis activity by grip.

references.citation: Boland MR, Spigelman T, Uhl TL (2008). The function of brachioradialis. J Hand Surg Am 33(10):1853–1859.
references.usedFor: Brachioradialis activity by grip (fine-wire EMG).

references.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, Moro T, Grigoletto D, Piccolo D, Paoli A (2018). Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
references.usedFor: Biceps and brachioradialis activity: dumbbell, straight-bar and EZ-bar curls.

references.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Toninelli N, Padovan R, Esposito F, Cè E (2023). Biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy. Sports 11(3):64.
references.usedFor: Biceps and brachioradialis activity by grip at matched effort (hammer and reverse curl factors).

references.citation: Mausehund L, Werkhausen A, Bartsch J, Krosshaug T (2022). Understanding bench press biomechanics — the necessity of measuring lateral barbell forces. J Strength Cond Res 36(10):2685–2695.
references.usedFor: Bench press: grip widths, touch points, sideways bar forces and moment arms the model is checked against.

references.citation: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, Sakurai H, Kusagawa Y, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci 23(7):1240–1250.
references.usedFor: Overhead triceps: more growth despite lower strength.

references.citation: Vigouroux L, Quaine F, Labarre-Vila A, Moutet F (2006). Estimation of finger muscle tendon tensions and pulley forces during specific sport-climbing grip techniques. J Biomech 39(14):2583–2592.
references.usedFor: Edge lift: open-hand and full-crimp finger postures, where the edge presses, the passive moment of the bent-back fingertip joint, and the reference tendon tensions; its FDP:FDS ratios and pulley loads are the model’s check.

references.citation: Schweizer A (2001). Biomechanical properties of the crimp grip position in rock climbers. J Biomech 34(2):217–223.
references.usedFor: Edge lift: maximum fingertip force per finger in the crimp and open grips, and how far the flexor tendons bowstring over the middle joint under load.

references.citation: An KN, Ueba Y, Chao EY, Cooney WP, Linscheid RL (1983). Tendon excursion and moment arm of index finger muscles. J Biomech 16(6):419–425.
references.usedFor: Edge lift: finger bone lengths and the FDP and FDS moment arms at the three finger joints.

references.citation: Murray WM, Delp SL, Buchanan TS (1995). Variation of muscle moment arms with elbow and forearm position. J Biomech 28(5):513–525.
references.usedFor: Biceps curl: how the biceps', brachialis' and brachioradialis' moment arms change with elbow angle, which sets the shape of their muscle weights.

references.citation: Folland J, Morris B (2008). Variable-cam resistance training machines: do they match the angle–torque relationship in humans? J Sports Sci 26(2):163–169.
references.usedFor: Leg extension: measured resistance profiles of knee-extension machines (mean of eight, and the two extremes) in place of an illustrative cam.

references.citation: Ono T, Higashihara A, Fukubayashi T (2011). Hamstring functions during hip-extension exercise assessed with electromyography and magnetic resonance imaging. Res Sports Med 19(1):42–52.
references.usedFor: Romanian deadlift: how the hamstrings' activity splits between biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus (surface EMG, stiff-leg deadlift).

references.citation: Messer DJ, Bourne MN, Williams MD, Al Najjar A, Shield AJ (2018). Hamstring muscle use in women during hip extension and the Nordic hamstring exercise: a functional magnetic resonance imaging study. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 48(8):607–612.
references.usedFor: Leg curl: how the hamstrings' activity splits between the heads in knee flexion (MRI, Nordic exercise); also a contrasting result for hip extension.

references.citation: Park S, Lim W (2023). Comparison of muscle activity of hamstrings as knee flexors and hip extensors and effect of tibial and hip rotation on the contribution of hamstrings. J Bodyw Mov Ther 34:1–5.
references.usedFor: Hamstrings: inner vs outer hamstrings in knee flexion and hip extension, and the shift towards the biceps femoris with the hip turned out (context for the per-head splits).

references.citation: Lin GT, Amadio PC, An KN, Cooney WP (1989). Functional anatomy of the human digital flexor pulley system. J Hand Surg Am 14(6):949–956.
references.usedFor: Edge lift: length and position of the A2 and A4 pulleys.

references.citation: Lin GT, Cooney WP, Amadio PC, An KN (1990). Mechanical properties of human pulleys. J Hand Surg Br 15(4):429–434.
references.usedFor: Edge lift: breaking loads of the A2 and A4 pulleys (cadaver), shown against the model’s pulley loads.

resources.name: wger.de
resources.usedFor: Exercise descriptions, images and the muscle-map SVGs, loaded at runtime with attribution; the exercise list this project started from (wger starter library).
